news.t: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start
news.sum: Tadhg Beirne, so often Ireland's 'Mr Dependable', leads the team's bid to improve on last week's win over Argentina against Fiji on Saturday.

news.t: England fly-half Harrison signs new Saracens deal
news.sum: England fly-half Zoe Harrison renews her contract with Saracens for the forthcoming Premiership Women's Rugby campaign.

news.t: 'You would have worried for the horses!' - Farrell on McNabney
news.sum: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell pays tribute to James McNabney who is in line to win his first international cap against Fiji on Saturday.

news.t: Vunipola exploring life after rugby with coaching role
news.sum: Former England prop Mako Vunipola talks about planning for his retirement by venturing into coaching at Leicester Tigers.

news.t: Beirne: Argentina win has to be 'foundation' for growth
news.sum: Tadhg Beirne insists Ireland will not rest on their laurels as he prepares to captain his country in Dublin for the first time in Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Fiji.

news.t: Townsend stresses individual responsibility as duo return
news.sum: Gregor Townsend stresses the importance of "individual responsibility" as Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn return to the Scotland XV against Australia.

news.t: Borthwick challenges Ojomoh to match talent with toughness
news.sum: Max Ojomoh must bring physicality, as well as his usual stardust, to England's backline, says head coach Steve Borthwick.

news.t: The driving-maul try machine - why rugby's steamroller gained traction

news.t: Lenihan: Nothing experimental about XV to face Fiji

news.t: All Blacks aim to eliminate threat of Wales flanker Morgan
news.sum: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie says they have spoken about targeting Wales' Lions flanker Jac Morgan in the Nations Championship encounter.

news.t: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams
news.sum: An Ospreys-commissioned report by experts at Sheffield Hallam University concludes Wales should retain four professional teams.

news.t: Fight for Ireland place 'a great thing' for Ryan
news.sum: Ireland second row James Ryan believes the competition for places is "a great thing" as Andy Farrell's side prepare to face Fiji in the Nations Championship in Dublin on Saturday.

news.t: Cheating, scandal and drama - Wales agony v All Blacks
news.sum: It is more than 70 years since Wales last beat New Zealand but the fixture has rarely failed to deliver drama.

news.t: McNabney rise a 'phenomenal story' - Farrell

news.t: Rugby Union Weekly
news.sum: Hear from George Ford and Eddie Jones as we preview round 5 of the Nations Championship.

news.t: 'Full steam ahead' as Ireland aim to lay down a mark

news.t: How and why Wales are relying on scrum-half Williams
news.sum: Wales head coach Steve Tandy says is a big demand on the workload of scrum-half Tomos Williams.

news.t: Eight-game ban for Ebbw Vale's Gregory over stamp
news.sum: Ebbw Vale lock Curtis Gregory must serve an eight-week ban for his brutal stamp on Llandovery's Joe Powell.

news.t: Farrell backs McNabney to make his mark on Test rugby
news.sum: Andy Farrell believes Ulster's James McNabney is ready to make the step up to Test level, after naming the 23-year-old in his squad for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Fiji.

news.t: Lawes recovering after hospital stay with infection
news.sum: Courtney Lawes says he spent 10 days in hospital after doctors found his infection markers were "through the roof" as he battled a serious illness.

news.t: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
news.sum: England scrum-half Alex Mitchell is facing a prolonged spell on the sidelines after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues.

news.t: Full-back Barrett leads New Zealand for first time
news.sum: Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time when he leads out much-changed All Blacks against Wales.

news.t: McNabney set for debut as Irish make seven changes
news.sum: Ulster's James McNabney is poised to make his Ireland debut off the bench as head coach Andy Farrell makes seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji.

news.t: Beirne captains Ireland, Timoney starts at 8 v Fiji
news.sum: Tadhg Beirne will captain Ireland in Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Fiji, while Nick Timoney has won the race to start at number 8 in the absence of Sean Jansen.

news.t: Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings

news.t: Painter 'couldn't sleep' after making Exeter return

news.t: Pollock starts alongside Ojomoh and Joseph in bold England side
news.sum: Free-scoring back row Henry Pollock will make only his second start for England in Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Japan.

news.t: Ryan: 'We're not thinking about South Africa'
news.sum: James Ryan insists Ireland are solely focused on Fiji, despite a crunch tie with South Africa looming next week.

news.t: England's Breach agrees new Saracens deal
news.sum: England winger Jess Breach agrees a new contract with Saracens ahead of the start of the 2026-27 Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) season.

news.t: Basham starts for Wales against All Blacks as Wainwright ruled out
news.sum: Wales number eight Taine Basham will start his first international for four years as he replaces the injured Aaron Wainwright against New Zealand.

news.t: Nations Championship: England recall Ford, Dupont at 10
news.sum: Steve Borthwick has opted to recall George Ford at out-half for Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Japan (4.40pm), in one of ten changes to their starting side.

news.t: 'We played the Traitors and I was terrible!'
news.sum: Joey Carbery admits he was "terrible" at the Traitors when the Leinster squad played the game in South Africa earlier this season.

news.t: Gibson-Park raring to go after disrupted start to season
news.sum: After a groin injury delayed his start to the season, Jamison Gibson-Park is excited to be "back in the mix" as he looks to kickstart his campaign.

news.t: 'It's what I want' - Carbery outlines Ireland dream
news.sum: In an interview with the Ireland Rugby Social, Joey Carbery outlines his international ambitions, recalls his Munster exit and speaks about incoming Leinster boss Noel McNamara.

news.t: The Ireland Rugby Social Podcast
news.sum: Joey Carbery on Ireland, France, his Leinster return, The Traitors and what's next.

news.t: Dupont picked at 10 amid France fly-half crisis

news.t: Irish workrate, backrow calls, and the hybrid player era

news.t: Ireland 'won't get into arm wrestle' with Fiji

news.t: Best calls for calm after winless Ulster start
news.sum: Ulster general manager Rory Best says "there's not a huge panic from my point of view" despite the province's winless start to the URC season.

news.t: Ulster's Timoney 'grateful' for Ireland chances
news.sum: Nick Timoney tells the BBC's Ireland Rugby Social podcast that he is relishing being a regular part of Ireland's matchday squads after having to be patient for his opportunities.

news.t: McCloskey happy to be the 'link guy' for others to shine
news.sum: For a few years, this week of an international window would be Stuart McCloskey's one real opportunity to shine in an Ireland shirt.

news.t: Timoney's stock continues to rise after breakout year
news.sum: Just as it looked like Nick Timoney had cemented his place as Ireland's first-choice openside flanker, he may be needed elsewhere.

news.t: Ireland deliver on promises, but South Africa loom large

news.t: Ireland's Jansen ruled out of Fiji and Bok games
news.sum: Sean Jansen is ruled out of the remainder of Ireland's Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's options at number eight.

news.t: Irish captain Sheehan ruled out of Fiji game
news.sum: Irish captain Dan Sheehan has been ruled out of the side's Nations Championship clash with Fiji on Saturday night.

news.t: England make massive step up in Australia victory
news.sum: In his latest column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on an impressive win for Steve Borthwick's side against Australia in the Nations Championship.

news.t: Rugby Union Weekly: England ease to victory over Australia
news.sum: Chris, Ashy and Paul Grayson get the on the whistle reaction from the Allianz

news.t: England ease pressure on Borthwick after big win over Australia
news.sum: England provide emphatic on-pitch backing for head coach Steve Borthwick as they score seven tries to swat aside a listless Australia at Allianz Stadium.

news.t: Seven-try New Zealand too strong for Scotland
news.sum: Watch highlights from Murrayfield as New Zealand prove too strong for Scotland in the Nations Championship

news.sum: Watch the highlights as Wales beat Japan 28-21 in their opening game of the Nations Championship in Cardiff.

news.sum: Ireland's November test window is off to a flying start, following Ireland's 30–point demolition of an off-colour Argentinian side on Friday night.

news.t: Nations Championship: Wales, All Blacks and Boks win

news.t: Argentina win 'a good start' - McCarthy
news.sum: Conor Murray and Gavin Andrews break down a six-try start for Ireland over Argentina in their November Nations Championship campaign.

news.t: Ireland going from strength to strength - Murray
news.sum: Former Ireland scrum-half Conor Murray says on the Ireland Rugby Social that he is impressed with how the Irish squad is progressing and their strength in depth.

news.t: 'Shackles off' for Porter on return from Irish absence
news.sum: Andrew Porter is back in a green shirt and thriving, having come through his 80th cap unscathed and close to his brilliant best.

news.t: Variety of scores the most pleasing aspect of win v Pumas
news.sum: With just over 10 minutes played at Aviva Stadium last night, there was a fear that Ireland's sluggish summer form would stretch into the winter.

news.t: Six tries and a big win - but were Ireland ruthless?
news.sum: Despite a six-try and 30-point win over Argentina, Andy Farrell and Tadhg Beirne admit Ireland could have been more ruthless in Friday's win.

news.t: Farrell: 'Some outstanding, really clinical stuff'
news.sum: A delighted Andy Farrell praised "some really clinical stuff" from his side's attack as they hammered Argentina 42-12 at Aviva Stadium.

news.t: Farrell delight at back three performance against Pumas
news.sum: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell praises the performances of hat-trick hero Hugo Keenan, Mack Hansen and Rob Baloucoune as the Irish secure a comfortable 42-12 bonus-point win over Argentina in Dublin.
